I am 68 years old and I have farmed this land in Quzhou County for over 50 years. I only finished primary school, but I know this soil and this weather better than any book. I have about 15 mu of good flat land. Every year I do the same thing my father did: I plant winter wheat in October, harvest it in early June, and immediately plant summer maize on the same plots. This double-cropping system works here because we have the water and the heat.

Right now it is early spring and my wheat is already in the ground. I grow Luyuan502, an improved wheat variety that my neighbors and I have used for years. It is reliable. Before sowing I always do rotary tillage to break up the soil. I put down compound fertilizer at sowing time, and now in spring I will topdress with urea when the wheat greens up — about 25 kg of nitrogen per mu. I do not bother buying straight phosphate or potash; the compound fertilizer has enough, and my soil has always been decent. I will irrigate three times before harvest: once now at green-up, once at jointing, and once at heading if the rain does not come. I also spray pesticides about four times for weeds, aphids, and rust.

After I harvest the wheat in June, I plant Denghai605 hybrid maize directly into the wheat stubble with no-tillage. Everyone here does it this way now — it saves fuel, time, and labor. I put compound fertilizer down at planting, and that is usually enough for the maize. I do not topdress with urea on maize anymore; at my age I want to make fewer trips to the field, and the compound does the job. I irrigate maize twice, in July and August. I spray pesticides three times for corn borers and weeds. 

I stopped growing cotton years ago. Cotton needs 14 or 15 sprays and hand-picking — too much work for an old man like me. I also do not fool around with vegetables or chili for the market; the prices jump up and down and I do not want the risk. Wheat and maize are safe because the machines do the sowing and harvesting, and I can sell them easily to the grain dealers who come to the village. If the weather is normal, I expect about 500 kg per mu of wheat and 550 kg per mu of maize.
